title: Observability and Incident Analysis
summary: You cannot fix what you cannot see. This lesson covers what to log for every LLM call, how to read latency percentiles, cost and error metrics, traces, quality measured in production, SLOs with error budgets, and how to run an incident and write a blameless postmortem.
objectives: Design a request log that lets you reconstruct any LLM call without storing more than you must
Compute p50, p95 and p99 from raw latencies and explain why averages mislead
Compute cost per request, cost per success and error rates with a confidence interval
Read a trace, find its critical path and decide what to optimise
Size a production evaluation sample and set an SLO, an error budget and burn-rate alerts
Run an incident and write a blameless postmortem with a timeline and action items
prerequisites: You should be comfortable with percentiles and the cost formula from [Choosing and Routing Models](/learn/production-systems/model-routing) and with the idea of an evaluation set ([Success Criteria](/learn/evaluation/success-criteria)). Latency terms (TTFT, TPOT) come from [Measuring Inference](/learn/inference-and-serving/measuring-inference).
